newsitem.title: UK: Nomura affirms Brazil CVRD BUY on results.
newsitem.headline: Nomura affirms Brazil CVRD BUY on results.

text.p: Nomura equity researchers affirmed their "Buy" rating for Brazilian mining giant CVRD on Thursday after its third quarter results came in broadly in line with expectations.
"We reiterate our Buy rating because strong prospects are intact, and maintain our earnings estimate for 1996, 1997 and 1998," it said in a statement released in London.
Companhia Vale do Rio Doce published January to September results on Wednesday, announcing net profits of 280 million reais compared with 209 million in the same period last year.
International investors are watching the company closely as it prepares for one of the biggest privatisations in Latin America's history.

The privatisation is expected to raise about $6 billion. The government hopes to auction 40 to 45 percent of the company's voting shares in February 1997 before selling further shares to investors via a global offering.
Nomura is estimating earnings per American Depositary Receipt of $1.06 in 1996, $1.42 in 1997 and $1.59 in 1998, and is posting a five-year earnings per share growth estimate of 21 percent.
Its stock price is also expected to increase steadily.
"Our target price for the stock is $28, a 33 percent increase for the next 12-18 months," Nomura analyst Steven Assis said.

While operating results were about what Nomura had expected, he said CVRD had suffered from lower than expected income from subsidiaries due to weak prices for aluminium and pulp and paper, and a higher than expected tax rate.
Although income tax maintained itself at 19 percent, the company's social contribution leapt to $7.4 million in the third quarter after $2.8 million in the first quarter of 1996, he added.
